description: Shared by tests/test_settings.py and gui/src/validate.test.ts so the agent and the GUI reject the same files. Each case applies edits to valid: set (a last path segment of - appends) or delete. schema lists the error paths; every error must sit at or under one of them. cross lists the exact cross-check messages, in order. v20 holds the three sections version 21 dropped (#782), as a new v0.1.0 file had them; each migrate_v20 case applies its edits to valid at version 20 with them and without team_queue (version 22's, #803), and the migration, the agent's and the GUI's, gives valid. Each migrate_v21 case applies its edits to valid at version 21 without team_queue, and the migration, the agent's and the GUI's, gives that file at version 22 with team_queue, the queue in the order of teams. moved is what the GUI then lists once (gui/src/movedOptions.ts): each moved value off the client's default as the client option that holds it and the value to set, NAME=VALUE as tools/live/bot.py run --option takes it (a switch Yes or No, a password input (set)), in the order the client sends them; a value no case or input of the client takes is not listed. skill_replacement_default is what a new team gets, no sinner listed, and the schema's default is the same. task_start holds the cases of the two rules that cross a task's options with the teams (the target floor's, a Luxcavation task's team): the agent checks them at that task's start (tests/test_task_options.py); the GUI checks neither, since the target floor and the team are client options it does not see (#779, #780). task is the task, options the client's NAME=VALUE options it starts with (assets/interface.json, its ExpTeam and ThreadTeam from tests/team_options.json: tests/client_options.py), edits the settings file's, cross that start's errors in order ([] when it passes them). too_old gives valid at an older version than the oldest both read and the one error both give for it, word for word. clean_gift_list cases give a list (want, keep, gorder; an unset gorder is {}) and what cleaning it gives (want, keep, dropped, gorder_head: a keyword's first ids, gorder_size: how many ids each keyword has).
